title.en: Contractions: no, na, do, and da

summary.en: Prepositions em ('in / on / at') and de ('of / from') always fuse with definite articles o, a, os, and as.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 1.

Within the first two scenes, Camila says *No primeiro dia eu sempre ando rápido*, Jorge answers *Na gaveta*, and Bianca introduces herself with *Eu sou a Bianca, da cozinha* while offering *Pãozinho fresco da manhã!*

In Portuguese, *em* ('in, on, at') and *de* ('of, from') never stand separately before the definite articles *o*, *a*, *os*, and *as*. Instead they blend into mandatory one-word contractions: *em* becomes *no*, *na*, *nos*, *nas* (*no primeiro dia*, *na gaveta*), and *de* becomes *do*, *da*, *dos*, *das* (*do quarto quatro*, *da cozinha*).

The same fusion happens with *por* (*pelo*, *pela*) and *a* (*ao*, *à*), which is why short words like *no*, *na*, *do*, and *da* anchor almost every Portuguese sentence.
